title: Coding-memory authority matrix
decision: TraceDecay owns coding context, exact repository/worktree/session identity, accepted Native facts, curated configuration, and final context assembly. Cognitive providers own only their provider-local state and return advisory candidates through capability ports.
global_invariants: Every durable state domain has exactly one canonical authority and one named canonical writer.
Current code in the exact admitted worktree is the highest-priority truth; memory never rewrites or contradicts it silently.
TraceDecay Native remains the sole authority for accepted explicit facts and their lineage, provenance, feedback, and trust transitions.
Session evidence remains a separate authority from accepted explicit facts.
Provider observations and provider cognitive state are namespaced by provider and exact coding scope.
Provider recall candidates are advisory, provenance-bearing, bounded, cancellable, and incapable of direct canonical mutation.
Curated rules are changed only through the TraceDecay configuration control plane.
The TraceDecay context compiler is the sole owner of final context assembly and emits typed partial or unavailable outcomes instead of silent fallback.
Repository, worktree, branch, agent-session, and provider namespaces are explicit and never inferred from the current working directory at request time.

namespace_axes.purpose: Separates user/profile-owned configuration, sessions, and optional profile memory.

namespace_axes.authority: TraceDecay project enrollment and registry authority
namespace_axes.purpose: Stable project owner for code, project sessions, and project memory.
Identifies the admitted repository independently of a path alias.
Separates linked worktrees that share one Git repository.

namespace_axes.authority: Git ref resolved for the exact worktree
namespace_axes.purpose: Pins branch-sensitive reads and context to an explicit ref when one exists.
Separates evidence and outcomes from concurrent coding-agent sessions.
Stable logical provider namespace independent of transport or process identity.
Separates provider installations, processes, accounts, or local stores.
Binds final context and terminal outcomes to one immutable request.
Deduplicates observations, feedback, and durable effects across retries.

authority_domains.canonical_writer: Exact admitted worktree filesystem; TraceDecay mutations publish only through the authorized atomic source-edit authority.
write_interfaces: authorized external editor or Git operation acting on the same exact worktree
read_interfaces: generation-pinned code graph and code-query ports
authority_domains.consistency_model: The filesystem bytes in the exact admitted worktree are authoritative. Source edits compare expected content and file identity, publish atomically, and fail on races or unsafe paths; derived indexes may lag but cannot replace source bytes.
authority_domains.failure_behavior: Fail closed on scope mismatch, unsafe path, symlink traversal, stale file identity, cancellation, deadline, or publication conflict. A stale graph is reported as unavailable/partial rather than treated as current code.
authority_domains.provider_semantics: Providers may cite code evidence but cannot write, shadow, or supersede current code truth.
prohibited_side_effects: provider output directly editing files
memory content overriding current source bytes
using a code index generation as canonical source truth
routing a request to a sibling worktree or branch

authority_domains.canonical_writer: TraceDecay project enrollment authority binding the durable project registry to the authoritative repository identity marker.
authority_domains.consistency_model: A project ID is accepted only with its registered root and authoritative repository identity. Missing or inconsistent markers fail closed; path strings alone are insufficient identity.
authority_domains.failure_behavior: Return typed resolution/unavailable errors on missing enrollment, marker mismatch, unrelated repository, or invalid project identity. Never synthesize a Git repository identity from CWD.
authority_domains.provider_semantics: Providers receive the admitted repository ID as immutable scope input and cannot mint or alias it.
prohibited_side_effects: provider-defined repository IDs
path-only repository identity
cross-repository recall
silently accepting a missing identity marker

authority_domains.canonical_writer: TraceDecay registered-scope admission over canonical roots and proved Git linked-worktree topology.
authority_domains.consistency_model: Each admitted request carries one canonical worktree ID. A linked sibling is accepted only when its Git common directory proves repository identity and its own canonical root supplies a distinct worktree identity.
authority_domains.failure_behavior: Deny unrelated sibling roots, relative paths, uncanonicalizable roots, or missing worktree identity. Do not collapse multiple linked worktrees into one context namespace.
authority_domains.provider_semantics: Provider state and recall must include the admitted worktree ID; repository-only provider buckets are insufficient for mutable coding context.
prohibited_side_effects: cross-worktree recall without explicit multi-root operation
deriving worktree identity from CWD
sharing mutable provider state across worktrees by default

authority_domains.canonical_writer: Git reference state for the exact admitted worktree.
read_interfaces: current_branch for the exact canonical root
authority_domains.consistency_model: Branch-sensitive context is pinned to the ref observed for the exact worktree. Detached/non-Git scopes carry no fabricated branch; consumers must handle absence explicitly.
authority_domains.failure_behavior: Return no branch or typed stale/unavailable state when the ref cannot be proved. Never reuse another worktree's active branch.
authority_domains.provider_semantics: Providers receive branch ref as part of scope when available; they cannot infer it from repository name or process CWD.
prohibited_side_effects: cross-branch recall presented as current
fabricating refs for detached or non-Git scopes
provider-controlled branch routing

authority_domains.canonical_writer: TraceDecay host admission and session/transcript ingest authority for the admitted profile or project session store.
authority_domains.consistency_model: Append/ingest receipts, source cursors, and exact session-store identity make replay idempotent. Project sessions retain repository/worktree/branch route; profile sessions use a disjoint reserved scope.
authority_domains.failure_behavior: Typed denied, unavailable, cancelled, timed-out, partial, or deferred outcomes. An unavailable session authority is not represented as an empty successful history.
authority_domains.provider_semantics: Normalized admitted observations may be mirrored to providers after canonical ingest, but provider state never replaces session evidence.
prohibited_side_effects: calling transcript observations accepted explicit facts
provider writes into TraceDecay session tables
cross-session or cross-project evidence leakage
empty success when the session authority is unavailable

authority_domains.canonical_writer: TraceDecay Native MemoryApplication over the owner-bound DatabaseFactStore/ProjectMemoryFactStore.
write_interfaces: automatic fact promotion after durable admission
authority_domains.consistency_model: Owner-bound append-only facts, lineage, provenance, idempotent operation identity, sanitization receipts, and durable mutation receipts. Search and relation graph data are derived from this authority.
authority_domains.failure_behavior: Fail closed on owner mismatch, invalid fact ID, privacy rejection, cancellation, deadline, conflict, unavailable store, or unknown effect settlement. No external provider fallback writes Native facts.
authority_domains.provider_semantics: Providers may return candidate evidence. Promotion into an accepted explicit fact requires a separate authorized Native command and durable receipt; there is no implicit promotion.
prohibited_side_effects: provider directly implementing or replacing ProjectMemoryFactStore
provider recall silently becoming a Native fact
multiple canonical fact writers
provider output changing Native feedback or trust

authority_domains.canonical_writer: TraceDecay product observation dispatcher writing one bounded idempotent provider-observation journal/outbox, implemented by the tracedecay-memory-observation crate.
write_interfaces: ObservationDispatchPortV1::append_admitted after canonical host or operation settlement
ObservationDispatchPortV1::record_withheld for a source event admission refused before journalling
ObservationRetentionPortV1::sweep_expired and forget_source for retention expiry and privacy deletion

ObservationRecoveryPortV1::accept_checkpoint and record_recovery_refusal for the accepted provider state identity and the bounded automatic repair counter; the acknowledged watermark is written only by the acknowledging receipt and can never be lowered
read_interfaces: ObservationJournalReaderV1::lease_pending for the provider delivery worker
ObservationJournalReaderV1::inspect and receipts_for for inspection and reconciliation
ObservationDispatchPortV1::replay_cursor and queue_pressure for restart recovery and backpressure
ObservationRecoveryPortV1::recovery_state and unacknowledged_frontier for restart recovery replay position and exact-effect verification against the provider checkpoint
authority_domains.consistency_model: At-least-once delivery from a durable journal, deduplicated by operation ID plus provider and exact scope. Provider acknowledgements are receipts; queue capacity and retry policy are bounded.
authority_domains.failure_behavior: Observer-mode dispatch failure is recorded and retryable but cannot alter prompts, Native facts, source edits, session ingest, or the already-settled host action. Capacity exhaustion returns a typed terminal outcome and never drops silently.
authority_domains.provider_semantics: The journal records what TraceDecay offered and what a provider acknowledged; it is not provider cognitive state and has no direct context influence.
prohibited_side_effects: unbounded observation queue
silent observation loss
observer failure changing canonical outcomes
provider adapter writing journal records without dispatcher admission

authority_domains.canonical_writer: TraceDecay ProjectNativeMemoryApplicationPort, writing one provider-local staged-observation store under the host-granted Native provider-state directory.
write_interfaces: NativeMemoryApplicationPort::observe for an admitted session.message_committed.v1 observation, committing the staged row durably before the success terminal is returned
per-scope retention eviction inside that same writer, which removes staged payload content and leaves a compact tombstone that still answers redelivery with the original committed-effect evidence
read_interfaces: NativeMemoryApplicationPort::recall, which merges staged rows with canonical Native fact candidates under one ProviderLimits.recall_candidates budget
provider-local inspection of staged rows for reconciliation and retention accounting
authority_domains.consistency_model: One durable row per admitted observation, committed before the observation is acknowledged. Identity is the admitted idempotency key plus a second uniqueness constraint on stable source identity (exact-scope digest, source authority, source event id, source event revision, sanitized payload digest), because the freshly derived idempotency key includes the registration revision and is therefore stable only for redelivery of one admitted journal row. Redelivery of a known key reproduces the original provider reference, receipt, and effect digest; the same key with a different kind or payload digest is a conflict. Payload bytes are stored exactly as admission sanitized them, with their digest and all seven exact-scope identity fields as explicit columns plus the exact-scope digest as immutable provenance.
authority_domains.failure_behavior: Fail closed before acknowledgement: a row that did not commit produces no committed-effect evidence and leaves the observation journal item pending for redelivery. Store unavailability, scope resolution failure, cancellation, deadline, and conflicting redelivery return typed terminals. No failure falls back to writing a canonical Native fact, and no recall answers with a row whose stored scope attestation it cannot reproduce.
authority_domains.provider_semantics: Derivative advisory state owned by the host's own Native provider. Staged rows are returned as advisory recall candidates attested under exact_coding_scope; they never replace TraceDecay's canonical admitted session/transcript evidence, which remains the authority for what a session said, and they never become an accepted Native fact except through the separate explicitly authorized promotion path. Exact-scope admission binds agent_session_id and resolved_scope_digest byte-for-byte, so staged recall is same-session only in this revision; the durable cross-session binding is tracked as tdmem-b8q.
prohibited_side_effects: writing memory_v2 or any canonical Native fact table from the staging path
acknowledging an observation before its staged row is durably committed
re-sanitizing, reshaping, or reconstructing the admitted payload bytes
emitting the observation envelope or raw payload as candidate content instead of the extracted message text
staged candidates starving canonical fact candidates or exceeding the single recall candidate budget
presenting a staged row as host-confirmed evidence or as a substitute for admitted session evidence
attesting a staged row under a scope binding wider than the exact scope it was recorded under

authority_domains.canonical_writer: The selected provider instance behind its capability adapter; TraceDecay never writes or interprets provider-internal representation directly.
authority_domains.consistency_model: Provider-defined persistence behind a versioned capability contract. TraceDecay supplies exact namespace, idempotency identity, deadline, cancellation, provenance, and bounded payloads but does not share Native tables.
authority_domains.failure_behavior: Typed unavailable, unsupported, cancelled, timed-out, partial, stale, or failed provider outcomes. No silent fallback and no fabricated readiness; provider failure cannot corrupt TraceDecay authorities.
authority_domains.provider_semantics: This is the provider's sole internal authority. Other providers and TraceDecay Native do not co-write it; provider-name branching stays inside registry/adapters.
prohibited_side_effects: TraceDecay depending on provider database schemas
one provider writing another provider's state
provider state treated as current code truth
provider state treated as accepted Native facts

read_interfaces: planned RecallProviderPortV1 invoked by the TraceDecay context compiler
authority_domains.consistency_model: One bounded response per admitted request, tied to provider ID, provider instance, exact scope, provider revision, source provenance, freshness evidence, score domain, deadline, and cancellation token.
authority_domains.failure_behavior: Typed unavailable/unsupported/cancelled/timed-out/partial/stale outcomes. Missing candidates are not reported as successful empty recall unless the provider explicitly completed with zero results.
prohibited_side_effects: direct source edit
direct Native fact mutation
direct configuration or curated-rule mutation
unlabelled insertion into final context
cross-scope candidate reuse
silent fallback to a different provider

authority_domains.canonical_writer: TraceDecay transactional configuration control plane under explicit authorization, revisioning, audit, and rollback.
write_interfaces: managed-skill materialization from an admitted configuration revision
authority_domains.consistency_model: Revisioned transactional configuration with explicit scope resolution, authorization, audit receipts, protected credentials, and pinned effective behavior digests. Generated skill files are projections of this authority.
authority_domains.failure_behavior: Typed conflict, denied, invalid, unavailable, cancelled, timed-out, or effect-unknown outcomes. The previous committed revision remains authoritative until a new revision settles.
authority_domains.provider_semantics: Providers may receive effective policy parameters but cannot modify rules, activate themselves, or materialize provider-specific public contracts outside the registry/adapter boundary.
prohibited_side_effects: provider changing configuration directly
provider output becoming a curated rule without explicit authorized mutation
generated skill files becoming an independent writer
silent activation on invalid or unavailable configuration

authority_domains.consistency_model: One immutable request-scoped assembly over exact admitted identity, pinned configuration/policy revisions, bounded source/session/fact/provider lanes, provenance on every item, deterministic ordering, and explicit coverage/terminal metadata.
authority_domains.failure_behavior: Code-truth admission failures fail the request. Optional evidence lanes return typed partial/unavailable status. Provider failure never fabricates context and never silently switches providers; the compiler records omission and provenance coverage.
authority_domains.provider_semantics: TraceDecay alone decides whether, where, and how advisory provider candidates appear. Candidates remain labelled with provider provenance and can be excluded for stale scope, policy, budget, or conflict with code truth.
prohibited_side_effects: provider constructing the final prompt/context envelope
provider candidate replacing code truth
unproven cross-worktree or cross-session material
dropping provenance or authority labels
silent fallback or fake complete coverage
context compilation mutating any source authority

cross_domain_rules.rule: Current code truth outranks every memory lane. Curated rules govern selection and disclosure but do not rewrite code truth. Accepted Native facts outrank session evidence and provider candidates as durable memory; provider candidates are always the lowest advisory lane.
Each durable domain has one canonical writer named in this matrix. Adapters and generated projections never become co-writers.
Session evidence or provider output becomes an accepted explicit fact only through a separate authorized Native fact command with sanitization, idempotency, lineage, and durable receipt.

Observer providers receive post-admission/post-settlement observations asynchronously through a bounded durable journal and cannot affect prompts, Native facts, source edits, configuration, or externally visible actions.

Project memory and provider operations bind project, repository, and worktree; branch, session, and provider identifiers are added whenever the source domain carries them. Missing identity fails closed.
Every compiled context item names its authority domain, source identity, observed revision/time, scope, freshness/coverage, and provider provenance where applicable.

Unavailable, unsupported, stale, cancelled, timed-out, partial, conflict, and effect-unknown outcomes remain distinct. Empty success is allowed only after an authority completed successfully with zero results.

Provider selection occurs only in the capability registry under pinned configuration: the memory.provider_recall_routing.v1 gate names the one active recall provider and MemoryFabric::route_active refuses observer, disabled, unregistered, or mis-revisioned registrations before any contact. Failure never switches providers or routes to Native implicitly; fallback dispatches only when the provider terminal is explicit_policy_only and the host FallbackRule::ExplicitPinned carries the identical policy id, revision, and target, otherwise the original reply is returned with a typed, observable FallbackDeclinedReason. Every routed result names the provider it is attributed to, so any fallback that does occur is explicit, observable, and separately accepted.
Provider-name branching is confined to registry and adapter construction. CLI, MCP, HTTP, dashboard, context compiler, and canonical stores depend only on capability contracts.

context_lane_order.role: authoritative inclusion, safety, disclosure, and behavior policy
admitted historical evidence for the exact session/scope
advisory cognitive candidates subject to all higher authorities
